meta.title: Curvatura
meta.description: An open research programme to take the warp drive from general relativity to engineering.

hero.title: Move space, not the ship.
hero.sub: An open programme to take the warp drive from general relativity to engineering.
hero.canvas: Expansion of volume elements around an Alcubierre bubble, computed in real time.

manifesto: In 1994 Miguel Alcubierre showed that general relativity allows a bubble that travels faster than light while nothing inside it does. The price was negative energy in impossible amounts. Thirty years later there are solutions with positive energy. This project starts there.

metric.title: One metric, three parameters.
metric.body: Move the parameters. Every value is computed by the project's own formula engine, with no precomputed tables.
metric.note: R in metres, σ in m⁻¹, v as a fraction of c. The negative sign is the central problem.

engine.title: Nine subsystems.
engine.body: The engine is broken down like any machine: what it produces, what feeds it, what holds it together and how it is tested.

items.name: Geometry
items.question: Which metric do we want to produce?
items.eq: theta = v_s * x_s / r_s * diff(f(r_s), r_s)

items.name: Energy conditions
items.question: Which stress-energy tensor does it require, and is it admissible?

items.name: Source
items.question: Which real matter produces that tensor?

items.name: Structure
items.question: How is the shell confined and supported?

items.name: Dynamics and control
items.question: How does it accelerate, steer and stop?

items.name: Semiclassical stability
items.question: Does it survive quantum effects?
items.state: Negative results in the superluminal regime

items.name: Medium
items.question: What happens to the surrounding particles?

items.name: Power
items.question: What is the mass and energy budget?

items.title: The bubble
items.text: Alcubierre writes an exact solution with arbitrary velocity and negative energy in the wall.

items.title: The quantum bound
items.text: Pfenning and Ford bound the wall thickness. The energy rises to cosmological orders.

items.title: Less energy
items.text: Van Den Broeck lowers the requirement by many orders of magnitude by reshaping the interior geometry.

items.title: Physical drives
items.text: Bobrick and Martire separate the impossible from the hard: subluminal bubbles with mass.

items.title: Positive energy
items.text: Fuchs and collaborators publish a constant-velocity solution that satisfies the energy conditions.

roadmap.title: Roadmap.
roadmap.body: Every phase has a measurable exit criterion. Nothing moves forward until it is met.

phases.name: Library
phases.text: Catalogue, verify and translate everything published. Equations in machine-readable form.

phases.name: Verified computation
phases.text: Reproduce every published result with relative error below 10⁻⁶ and an automated test.

phases.name: Design space
phases.text: Optimise metric families: minimum mass, positive energy, bounded stress.

phases.name: Physical sources
phases.text: Find matter with a real equation of state that produces the metric.

phases.name: Dynamics
phases.text: Simulate start and stop in numerical relativity, with their gravitational-wave signature.

phases.name: Laboratory analogue
phases.text: Build an acoustic bubble in a water channel and measure it.

phases.name: Prototype
phases.text: Preliminary design open to third-party review, only if a viable source exists.

lab.title: Lab
lab.body: An AI-powered research lab. Pose a problem: the AI searches the library, computes with the project's equations and tells you what survives. Below, the state of the research and the numerical tools.
lab.coreBody: Expansion field computed in Rust compiled to WebAssembly. Click the map to drop a particle and follow its geodesic.
lab.pythonBody: The repository's physics/ package running on Pyodide. Edit and run.
lab.formulaBody: Type an expression. The engine draws it, differentiates it and evaluates it.
lab.pythonSize: One-off download of about 30 MB, cached afterwards.
lab.installingNative: Installing Python 3.12, numpy, sympy, scipy and matplotlib…
lab.nativeBody: Python 3.12 installed in the app folder, with the physics/ package. Faster than the browser and without its memory limit.

ai.title: AI researcher
ai.body: Ask as you would ask a colleague. The AI searches the ~3,400 papers in the library, opens the ones that matter, computes every figure with the formula engine and ends with a verdict: alive, clashes with a law, or discarded.
ai.keyHint: The key is stored only on this device and goes straight to Anthropic. It never touches Curvatura's servers.
ai.keyGet: Create a key in the Anthropic console
ai.keyBad: The key is not valid or has no access. Check it and try again.
ai.placeholder: Pose a problem, an idea or a figure you want to check…
suggestions: What is the minimum mass of a subluminal positive-energy shell at 0.02 c? Compare with Fuchs 2024.

What wall thickness do quantum inequalities demand for a 100 m bubble at 0.1 c?
Is there any way around the null energy condition outside the Natário class? Search the library.

account.title: Account
account.body: Rate papers with stars and, if you have training or work in the field, give honourable mentions.
account.intro: Rating requires a verified account. We use ORCID, the researcher identifier: we never store passwords.
account.notConfigured: ORCID sign-in will be enabled shortly.
account.stepsTitle: How the honourable mention is verified
steps: Sign in with ORCID. Your identity is verified by ORCID.
Enter your bachelor's, master's, postgraduate, PhD or job in physics, engineering or a related field. If your institution has confirmed it on ORCID, it is approved instantly.
Otherwise attach the diploma or contract. A reviewer checks that the document and the institution are real and replies here.
account.document: Document (PDF, PNG or JPG, max 5 MB)
account.documentHelp: Required unless your institution confirmed it on ORCID. Deleted when the review ends; we only keep its fingerprint.
account.none: You have not sent any yet.
account.onWeb: Manage your account on the website
account.privacy: Documents are only seen by the review team and are deleted when the review closes.
account.resultApproved: Verified with your ORCID record. You can now give honourable mentions.
account.resultPending: Request received. We will let you know here when it is reviewed.
